header.title: pLondon BM EA 10477 (pNu): AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Book of the Dead
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:egy:tla:tb:plondon-bm-ea-10477-pnu:translit, from the Thesaurus Linguae Aegyptiae (2018), in Simon Schweitzer's AED-TEI (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.
header.availability: CC BY-SA 4.0, as its source requires: credit the Thesaurus Linguae Aegyptiae (2018), in Simon Schweitzer's AED-TEI and this AI translation, and share adaptations under the same licence.

notes.125.1: [...] stands where the edition omits or has lost the owner's name (Nu). 125.6: {zꜣw,t} is deleted by the editor and [jr,j.w] restored. 125.7: zꜣ,tj Mr,tj is uncertain: 'two daughters' and 'two eyes', or the Merty goddesses. 125.10: r[m]ṯ.pl sits loosely at the end of the line. 125.13: 'what is not' (jw,tt) probably means wrongdoing. 125.15: sense uncertain, probably labour exacted beyond what was due. 125.29-30: nk/nkk and dꜣdꜣ are sexual verbs whose exact sense is disputed; nkk is usually taken as the passive partner in sex between men. 125.35: nmḥ as in 125.17; 'tampered with' is approximate. 125.38: qs.pl is normally 'bones'; perhaps an error for a word for reed-beds. 125.39: ẖꜣ.w,t, 'lagoons', is uncertain. 125.46: 'four times' (zp-4) is an instruction to repeat the phrase.
notes.125.52: Many of the judges' names and places are of uncertain sense and are rendered literally or kept as names (Ruty, Qereti, Anedjuy, Wamemty, Kenemti, Tem-sep, Ihy). Uncertain words: 125.59 ḫtḫt 'going backwards' (or a place); 125.61 ḫmi̯.y 'Destroyer'; 125.62 knj 'sullen'; 125.63 ḏꜣi̯.t, queried by the edition; 125.64 ḥnw,yt 'mischief'; 125.65 ꜥm-jb 'swallow the heart', an idiom of uncertain meaning; 125.68 ḥnb 'land allotments'; 125.69 smtmt 'eavesdrop'; 125.70 šmi̯ 'go about', with no object; 125.72 ḏw ḏw,t=f; 125.75 ḥrw 'terror'; 125.78 ṯrm 'make weep'; 125.81 sr ḫrw; 125.89 šfw,t 'being puffed up'; 125.90 sṯni̯.yt 'distinctions'; 125.93 sꜣt 'belittle'. 125.82: 'I have not washed a god' is odd and may be corrupt. 125.84: the negative is taken to cover 'seen evil'. 125.89 and 125.93 name no place of origin. 125 (second confession): nkk is usually taken as the passive partner in sex between men; the exact sense is disputed.
notes.125.158: 125.159: wꜣḏ taken as the papyrus-sceptre and qmꜣ.w as 'thrown'; it could be 'the green rushes of the canal'. 125.166, 169: ꜥr,yt, 'jamb', may be 'lintel'. 125.168: ḥnk,w, 'offering', is uncertain. 125.171: ꜥnḫ,t, 'Living One', is uncertain. 125.175: ḥpt.w, 'bolts', is uncertain. 125.185: gr, rendered 'and', may be 'be silent'. 125.189: bz.w, 'image', is uncertain. 125.190: wnpp,t is unidentified. 125.196, 207: the doorkeeper's words are read as two questions. 125.226: ḫrw-fj sw is obscure; taken as 'so he says'. 125.233: n ḥntꜣ is obscure. 125.234: the line opens with n, taken as 'for', since a negative would contradict the promise.
notes.30A.10: 30A.11: r-jm,j-[w]t[j], 'among', is partly restored. 30B.2: jb and ḥꜣ,tj are two words for the heart, rendered 'heart' and 'breast'; 'twice' (zp-2) marks the phrase for repetition.
notes.63B.5: This long version of spell 64 is often obscure; many lines are rendered word for word. 63B.6: smj,w and ḏsf are unidentified; mj may be 'come' or 'like'. 64.3: nꜣ bkꜣ ḥr[,t] [r] msi̯.t=f is obscure; bkꜣ may be 'morrow' or 'be pregnant'. 64.4: bjk.du 'two falcons' and m n-sw.du are uncertain. 64.5: wr wr,t.j is uncertain. 64.10: the numbers and zš zmꜣ are obscure. 64.11: rʾ-6, 'one sixth', perhaps a festival. 64.15: nzp.w is unidentified. 64.16: the whole line is obscure (db.wj 'two horns'?, ḥn,t 'canal'?). 64.17: sense uncertain. 64.21: nsq, 'bite', is a guess. 64.24: sꜣ, 'protection', may be 'back'. 64.25: ḏꜣi̯,wt 'wrongdoing' and zmꜣ,yt.du 'two confederacies' are uncertain. 64.31: n-mḥ≡f taken as a name. 64.33: gš, 'reed-bank', is uncertain. 64.38: sꜣr.yw, 'those in need', may be 'the wise'. 64.41: sḫ.wj, 'two halls', is uncertain. 64.44: gꜣgꜣ and nn,wt are uncertain. 64.45: rw ḫ[y] is uncertain. 64.50: šnj-tꜣ, 'Encircler of the Earth', may be 'hair of the earth'.
notes.17.175: 17.177: wdd sṯꜣ[,w], 'shoots darts', is a guess. 17.180: Wenet is unidentified. 17.181: Shenyt is unidentified. 17.182: sꜣt[.w], 'impure', is uncertain. 17.183: mds taken as 'the Sharp One'.
notes.125.127: 125.128: ṯꜣm,t n.t ḥr=sn, 'covering on their faces', is uncertain; the sense may be that they show no pity.
notes.6.3: 6.3: the clause jsṯ ḥwi̯ n=f sḏb is uncertain. 7.3: wꜥ mnḥ, 'One of wax', is uncertain. 7.6: n j:tm gnn read as 'of one who does not grow limp', with a play on Atum's name. 7.7: gm,wt is unidentified.
notes.17.145: 17.152: sjꜣṯ,j, 'butcher', is uncertain; the verb means 'cheat, diminish'.
notes.17.163: 17.163: sṯꜣ,w is unidentified. 17.166: mḏd,w taken as a name; the verb mḏd means 'press, strike'. ns, 'flame', is literally 'tongue'.
notes.22.8: 22.9: only the verb, restored as 'quench', and its suffix survive. 23.1: 'r ḥkꜣ =f' ('for his magic') and 'r ẖr-nṯr' ('to/in the necropolis') read oddly in a spell title. 23.3: badly broken; jr,j.w ('belonging to, which are on') has lost its object.
notes.23.10: The last phrase (psḏ,t [t]w nṯr.pl =sn dmḏ.y) is uncertain; literally '[th]is Ennead, their gods united'.
notes.29.1: 29.4: 'n ḫnd.w' is obscure: 'for treading', 'to the striders', or a verb 'I stride'.
notes.30B.12: 30B.13: ṯni̯.t 'distinction, exaltation' (the verb can also mean 'grow old'). 31.2: swy is unidentified, apparently a name or epithet of the crocodile. 31.5: jmi̯ =j ḏd is read with the negative verb ('lest I speak'); 'let me speak' is also possible. 31.7: Bedti may mean 'He of the emmer'. 31.9-11: šni̯ 'encircle, enclose' can also mean 'conjure'. 31.13: ḏwf.t is unidentified. 31.14: bqs,w and the construction of the address are obscure; 'fixed' is a guess.
notes.34.3: 34.3 gives a variant for the preceding 'mound of Denpu'; rnp,yt may be 'fresh plants' or 'years'. 35.2: Busiris (Djedu) has a restored final [j], with which the word may instead be Djedwy, 'the Two Djed-pillars'; ṯz-pẖr 'and the reverse' marks that the address may be read both ways (Busiris says it to Shu); ḫnm 'unite with' may also be 'nurse'.
notes.38B.12: 40.3: literally 'far, your face'. 40.5: 'jnk m tr' is ambiguous: 'I am in season' or 'Who, then, am I?'. 40.6: 'n njs =f' may be 'without his being summoned' or 'to the one who summons him'.
notes.90.3: 'm mꜣs,t.pl =kj' is obscure: 'in your knees' or 'upon your knees'; =kj is a dual-looking form of 'your'. swḫꜣ 'foolishness' may also be 'forgetfulness'.
notes.108.4: 108.4: ḫt is the rod measure of 100 cubits. 108.8: 'wbḫ n bšw' is unclear; bšw is elsewhere 'vomit' (cf. 108.16). 108.10: the snake's name, jm,j hm =f, is uncertain. 108.11: ꜥḥꜥj is taken as the 'halt' of the sun's bark (cf. 108.12); it may be a time of day. 108.13: sdgꜣ,wt 'hiding, concealment' is obscure. 108.15, 108.19: bjꜣ is copper or iron. 108.17: m-ḏr,j 'near' as in the following line of the papyrus.
notes.141.127: 141.127: Heni is an unidentified place. The names of the keepers, guards and heralds are translated literally and several are uncertain: 144.7 sqd ḥr ('Travelling Face'); 144.8 ꜣsb ('Blazing One', the editor's correction of sꜣbs); 144.16 ꜣd,w ('the Aggressor', perhaps the crocodile); 144.19 ꜣẖb,w, left as a name; 144.20 ꜣ,t ('onslaught' or 'moment'); 144.22 jkn tʾ; 144.28 ḫmi̯,yw ('destroyers'). 144.14 and 144.28 could also be read 'Repeller of Face' with what follows as a second name.
notes.145.57: 145.57: jh[,w] =s ('her harm') is uncertain; bs.w and pꜥw are taken as words for flame.
notes.149.99: 149.99: 'twt js n wr' is taken as '[I am] the likeness of the great one'. 149.100: pꜣq.w may be thin loaves or fine linen. 149.101: ksj zpꜣ, 'the bowing centipede' (?), is uncertain. 149.102-103: ḫꜣy,tj.w ('slaughterers') and ḏꜣy,tj.w ('adversaries') are classes of hostile demons.

nodes.text: O these ushabtis, if the Osiris [...], justified, is counted off to do any work that is done there in the necropolis — for an obstacle is set there for him, as for a man at his duties — count yourself in at any time that work is done there, to cultivate the fields, to irrigate the riverbanks, to ferry the sand of the West to the East.
“I will do it; here I am,” you shall say.
Spell for passing by the evil coil of Apophis.
Recitation by [...], justified:
O One of wax, who takes by robbery, who lives on the inert, I will not grow weary for you;
I will not grow limp for you;
your poison will not enter my limbs;
my limbs are the limbs of Atum, of one who does not grow limp for you;
your *gemut* will not enter these limbs of mine.

O Ra who is in his egg, who shines in his disk, who rises in his horizon, who swims upon [his firmament] [...], who sails upon the supports of Shu, who gives breezes with the blast of his mouth, who brightens the Two Lands with [his radiance], may you rescue [...], justified, from that god, great and mysterious of form, whose eyebrows are the two arms of the balance [on that night] of the reckoning of the robber.
Who is he?
It is He-who-Brings-his-Arm.
As for that night of [reckoning] the robber, it [is the] night [of the flame] of the slain,
the one who puts lassoes on the wrongdoers at his slaughter-block that cuts off bas.
Who is he?
[It is] Shesmu.
He is the butcher of Osiris.
Another version: it is Apophis.
May you rescue [...], justified, from those keepers of the *setjau*, the butchers, sharp of fingers, painful in beheading, who are in the following of Osiris.
They shall not have power over me,
I shall not go down into their cauldrons,

for I know them, I know that *Mededu* who is among them, of the house of Osiris, who shoots with his eye without being seen, who goes round the sky with the flame of his mouth, who announces Hapi without being seen.
O Ra-Atum, lord of the Great Mansion, sovereign of all the gods, may you rescue [...], justified, from that god whose face is a hound's and whose eyebrows are people's;
another version: his skin is that of people;
who lives on the slain, keeper of that bend of the lake of fire, who swallows corpses, who snatches hearts, who shoots darts without being seen.
Who is he?
Swallower of Millions is his name.
He is in the Lake of Wenet.
As for that lake of fire, it is the one between Naref and Shenyt.
As for anyone who treads upon it, being impure, he falls to the slaughter.
Another version: the Sharp One is his name.
[He is] the doorkeeper [of the West].
Another version: Babi is his name.
He is the one who guards that bend of the West.
Another version: He-who-is-over-his-Affair is his name.
O Lord of Terror, chief of the Two Lands, [lord of blood], fresh of slaughter-blocks, who lives on entrails!
[May you rescue] [...], justified, from that god who seizes bas, who licks up corruption, who lives on putrefaction, keeper of darkness, who is in the gloom, whom those who are in inertness fear.
Who is he?
It is Seth.

O Khepri in the midst of his barque, primeval one whose body is eternity, may you rescue [...], justified, from those keepers of inspection to whom the Lord of All has given power to keep watch over his enemies, who inflict slaughter in the slaughter-places, who have no going out from their watch.
Their knives shall not be sent against me,
I shall not enter their slaughter-places,
I shall not go down into their slaughter-blocks,
I shall not sit in their fish-traps.
I have done what my heart desires in the Island of Fire.
I [quenched] [...]
Spell for opening the mouth of [...] for his magic in the necropolis.
Words spoken by [...], [justified]:
[...] which belong to [...], by my town god.
As for any magic or any word that is spoken against me, the gods shall rise up against them, the whole Ennead, [th]is Ennead whose gods are gathered together.
Spell for not letting the heart of [...], justified, be taken from him in the necropolis. He says:
Back, you messenger of every god!
Is it for this heart of mine of the living that you have come?
This heart of mine of the living shall not be given to you for treading (?).
May you commend me to Neheb[kau],
for he is joined among the great ones, enduring on earth, not dying in the West, being a spirit there.
To be said over it as magic:
My heart of my mother — twice — my breast of my forms: do not stand against me as a witness,
do not oppose me as a witness,
do not oppose me in the tribunal,
do not show hostility against me before the Keeper of the Balance.
You are my ka that is in my body, Khnum who makes my limbs sound.
Do not tell lies against me in the presence of the great god.
See, your distinction exists.
Spell for repelling the crocodile that comes to take away the magic of [...], justified, from him in the necropolis. He says:
Back, you! Retreat! Back, you, Sui!
Do not come against me:
I live by my magic.
Lest I speak this name of yours to the great god who causes you to come:
'Messenger' is the name of one,
'Bedti' is the name of the other.
Your face is toward Maat.
The sky has enclosed with its hours,
magic has enclosed his lies,
my mouth has enclosed the magic that is in it.
My teeth are of flint,
my molars are of *djufet* (?).
O you who sit, whose eye is fixed (?) on my magic, do not take it, crocodile who lives by magic!
Spell for repelling a snake.
Words spoken by [...], justified:
Variant: 'the mound of the fresh plants'.
Keep far from me!
I am Mafdet!
Spell for [...], justified, not being eaten by a snake in the necropolis. He says:
O Shu, so says Busiris, and the reverse! [He who is] under the headcloth of Hathor: they unite with Osiris.
I live in Busiris,
I live again after death, like Ra every day.
Spell for repelling the Swallower of the Ass.
Words spoken by [...], justified:
Keep your face away!
Do not eat me, for I am pure.
I am [one who is] in season (?),
who comes of himself, unsummoned.
I have climbed up in the radiance.
Khnum, foremost of the *smiu*, like one who cuts *djesef*, travelling after this road by which I have come forth.
Spell for knowing the spells of going forth, in a single spell.
Recitation by [...]:

I am Yesterday, he of the Morrow, on the way [to] his birth at another time, mysterious of ba, who made the gods, who gives offerings to the Westerners, western one of the sky, rudder of the East, lord of two faces, who sees his rays, lord of uplifting, who comes forth from the twilight.
O his two falcons, who are over their council, who hear matters as those who belong to him, the foreleg tied to the neck, the rump upon the head of the West:
give me what is within, great one of the two great ones;
do not attack me.
I weep for what I have seen.
I know the word concerning your name;
you shall act for the needs of the spirits.
It is millions, it is hundreds of thousands, as 1,200 with respect to it, as 12 cubits in a joined *zesh*, giving one by one there.
It is one sixth, the portion of the Foremost of the Duat, the hour of felling the rebel, from which one comes justified.
These are what is in the forecourt of the Duat:
seven strides at his coming forth.
This is my protection in the presence of my power.
The blood is cool, the *nezepu* are fresh.
I have parted the two horns in my uniting, in the canal against me.
Mysterious of forms are those who would repel me.
You who are on your bellies, let the eye swallow its tears.
O Igeret, O Igeret, open what is sealed for me;
give me the good roads, that I may pass.
Who then is the one who bites in the West?
I am the Foremost of Rosetjau, who enters in his name and comes forth as the Seeker, lord of the millions of the earth, who made his name.
The pregnant woman has laid down her burden;
the protection is sealed upon the wall.
It is the overturning of wrongdoing, fallen upon the back of the Benu bird upon the two confederacies.
Horus has given him his eye;
his face is bright at daybreak.
I do not vomit;
I come into being as a lion;
Shu acclaims me.
I am He-is-not-Seized.
How good is the mooring of the Weary-Hearted!
He makes a resting place of the reed-bank.
Behold, the going forth!
I am the Lord of Life;
this is my arrival.
I go forth from the great doorway of the city of Osiris.
Behold, your portion is with those in need.
I have embraced the sycomore,
the sycomore has sheltered me.
The two halls of the Duat have been opened for me.
I have come to see the One-in-his-Coil face to face, eye to eye,
seeking breath at his coming forth.
How astonished I am at these before me!
O lion, [child] who is in Wetjenet, you are in me
and I am in you;
your form is my form.
I am the flood;
Great Black is my name.
My forms are the forms of Khepri, the Encircler of the Earth, Atum — twice.
I entered as one who does not know,
I have come forth as an excellent spirit.
I shall be seen in my form of a man for ever.
It is going forth by day: a man is not turned back on the road of the Duat in entering and in going forth, and he takes on forms as whatever he desires.
It is the ba of a man not dying again.
As for one who knows this spell, he is justified on earth and in the necropolis;
he does all that the living do.
It is, moreover, a great protection of the god.
This spell was found in the foundation of the One in the Henu-barque by the overseer of builders of the wall, in the time of the Majesty of the King of Upper and Lower Egypt Khasty, justified.
It is a secret image, not to be seen, not to be looked upon.
This spell is to be recited [by one who is] clean and pure, not eating goats or fish, not approaching women.
Spell for going forth by day.
Recitation by [...], justified:
I have felled my enemies on earth,
and my corpse has been buried.
As for anyone who knows this spell, he will go forth by day;
he will not be turned back at any gate in the necropolis;
he will take his form as a swallow.

O you who cut off heads and sever necks, who put foolishness into the mouth of the spirits because of the magic that is in their bodies: you shall not see me with these two eyes of yours with which you see, in your knees (?).
It is 300 rods in its length and 150 rods in its breadth.
Sobek, lord of Bakhu, is in the east of that mountain;
his temple is of carnelian.
A snake is on the brow of that mountain;
it is 30 cubits in its length, 8 cubits of its forepart are of flint, gleaming with *beshu* (?).
[...], justified, knows the name of that snake which is on its mountain:
'He Who Is in His Fire' (?) is its name.
Now after the halt (?), it turns its eyes [against] Ra,
and then a halt comes about in the bark
and a great hiding (?) in the course of the voyage.
Then it swallows seven cubits of the great water.
Then Seth makes a lance of metal fly against it,
and then he makes it spew out all it has swallowed.
Then Seth places himself near it
and then he says as magic:
Retreat before the sharp metal that is in my hand!
To be said on reaching this Hall of the Two Truths, separating [...], justified, from every wrong he has done, and seeing the faces of the gods.
Recitation by [...]:
Hail to you, great god, lord of the Two Truths!
I have come to you, my lord, I have been brought
so that I may see your beauty.

I know you, I know your name, I know the names of the forty-two gods who are with you in this Hall of the Two Truths, who live on [those who do] evil, who swallow their blood on that day of reckoning characters before Wennefer.
Behold, Two Daughters, Two Eyes, Lord of the Two Truths is your name.
Behold, I have come to you;
I have brought you Maat,
I have driven away for you the wrongdoing of people.
I have not impoverished [my] fellows.
I have not done wrong in the place of truth.
I have not known what is not.
I have not done evil.
I have not, at the start of every day, made work beyond what was to be done for me.
My name has not reached the office of the overseers.
I have not deprived the orphan of his property.
I have not done what the gods abhor.
I have not slandered a servant to his superior.
I have not caused pain.
I have not caused hunger.
I have not caused weeping.
I have not killed.
I have not ordered killing.
I have not caused anyone suffering.
I have not diminished the food offerings in the temples.
I have not damaged the loaves of the gods.
I have not taken away the cakes of the spirits.
I have not copulated with a *nkk* [a passive male partner].
I have not fornicated.
I have not diminished the measure.
I have not diminished the aroura.
I have not falsified the fields.
I have not added to the weights of the balance.
I have not tampered with the plummet of the scales.
I have not taken milk from the mouths of children.
I have not driven the flocks from their pastures.
I have not trapped birds of the bones of the gods.
I have not caught fish of their lagoons.
I have not held back water in its season.
I have not built a dam against flowing water.
I have not quenched a fire at its time.
I have not neglected the days for the choice cuts.
I have not turned back the herds from the god's property.
I have not opposed a god in his procession.
I am pure — four times.
My purity is the purity of that great Benu bird that is in Herakleopolis,
for I am that nose of the lord of breath who gives life to all the people on that day of filling the Wedjat-eye in Heliopolis, in the second month of Peret, the last day.
I am one who has seen the filling of the Wedjat-eye in Heliopolis.
O Wide-of-Stride, who comes forth from Heliopolis, I have not done wrong.
O Embracer-of-Fire, who comes forth from Kheraha, I have not robbed.
O Nose-One, who comes forth from Hermopolis, I have not been greedy.
O Swallower-of-Shades, who comes forth from the cavern, I have not stolen.
O Terrible-of-Face, who comes forth from Rosetjau, I have not killed people.
O Ruty, who comes forth from the sky, I have not damaged the measure.
O His-Eyes-are-Fire, who comes forth from Letopolis, I have not done crookedness.
O Flame, who comes forth going backwards, I have not stolen the god's offerings.
O Bone-Breaker, who comes forth from Herakleopolis, I have not told lies.
O Destroyer, who comes forth from the Shetayt-shrine, I have not plundered.
O Green-of-Flame, who comes forth from Memphis, I have not been sullen.
O His-Face-Behind-Him, who comes forth from the cavern of crossing (?), I have not taken away food.
O Qereti, who comes forth from the West, I have not made mischief.
O Hot-of-Foot, who comes forth from the twilight, I have not swallowed my heart.
O White-of-Teeth, who comes forth from the Fayum, I have not transgressed.
O Blood-Eater, who comes forth from the slaughter-place, I have not slaughtered sacred cattle.
O Entrail-Eater, who comes forth from the Court of Thirty, I have not been greedy for land allotments.
O Lord of Maat, who comes forth from the Two Truths, I have not eavesdropped.
O Wanderer, who comes forth from Bubastis, I have not gone about.
O Anedjuy, who comes forth from Heliopolis, I have not quarrelled except over my own property.
O Evil-of-his-Evil, who comes forth from Andjet, I have not copulated with a *nkk* [a passive male partner].
O Wamemty, who comes forth from the place of execution, I have not fornicated.
O He-who-Sees-What-He-Has-Brought, who comes forth from the house of Min, I have not had sex with a man's wife.
O Chief of the Great Ones, who comes forth from the Acacia, I have not caused terror.
O Lord of Letopolis, who comes forth from Xois, I have not been hot of mouth.
O Raiser-of-Voice, who comes forth from Weryt, I have not made myself deaf to words of truth.
O Child, who comes forth from Heqa-andj, I have not made another weep.
O Kenemti, who comes forth from Kenmet, I have not reviled.
O Bringer-of-his-Offering, who comes forth from Sais, I have not been violent.
O Announcer-of-Voices, who comes forth from Wenes, I have not been hasty of heart.
O Lord of Faces, who comes forth from Nedjefet, I have not transgressed my nature; I have not washed a god.
O Accuser, who comes forth from Wetjenet, I have not been loud of voice in speech.
O Lord of the Two Horns, who comes forth from Asyut, I have not done wrong [or] seen evil.
O Nefertem, who comes forth from Memphis, I have not cursed the king.
O Tem-sep, who comes forth from Busiris, I have not waded in the water.
O He-who-Acts-by-his-Heart, who comes forth from Tjebu, my voice has not been loud.
O Ihy, who comes forth from Nun, I have not reviled a god.
O Flourisher-of-the-People, I have not been puffed up.
O Allotter-of-Good, who comes forth from his mansion, I have not made distinctions.
O Nehebkau, who comes forth from his cavern, my portion has not been great except through [my own] property.
O Holy-of-Head, who comes forth from his shrine, there is no reviling of the god in me.
O Bringer-of-his-Arm, I have not belittled the god of my town.
Recitation by [...], justified:
Hail to you, you gods who are in this Hall of the Two Truths!
I know you, I know your names.
I will not fall to your slaughter,
you will not report my wrong to this god whom you follow,
no case of mine will come before you;
you will speak truth concerning me before the Lord of All,
for I have done what is right in Egypt.
I have not reviled a god;
no case of mine has come before the king of his day.
Hail to you who are in this Hall of the Two Truths, who have no lie in their bodies, who live on truth, who swallow truth before Horus who is in his disk!
Rescue me from Babi, who lives on the entrails of the great ones on that day of the great reckoning.
Behold, I have come to you:
I have no wrongdoing,
I have no crime,
I have no evil,
there is no witness [against] me,
there is none against whom I have done anything.
I live on truth,
I swallow truth.
I have done what people speak of and what the gods are pleased with.
I have satisfied the god with what he loves.
I have given bread to the hungry, water to the thirsty, clothes to the naked, a ferry-boat to the boatless.
I have made god's offerings for the gods and invocation offerings for the spirits.
So rescue me,
so protect me.
I have come here to bear witness to truth, to set the balance in its place within Igeret.

O High One upon his standard, lord of the atef-crown, whose name has been made as Lord of Breath, rescue me from these messengers of yours who inflict injuries, who bring about punishments, who have no covering on their faces.
I have quenched the fire,
I have broken the papyrus-sceptre, thrown into the canal.
Come, then,
enter by this door of this Hall of the Two Truths,
for you know us.
We will not let you enter past us, say the door-posts of this door,
unless you tell our name.
Plummet of the Place of Truth is your name.
I will not let you enter past me, says the jamb of this door,
unless you tell my name.
Offering of the Raising of Maat is your name.
I will not let you enter past me, says the jamb of this door,
unless you tell my name.
Living One of Sobek, Lord of Bakhu, is your name.
I will not open for you, says this door,
unless you tell my name.
Breast of Shu, which he set before Osiris, is your name.
We will not let you enter past us, say the bolts,
unless you tell our name.
Children of the Cobras is your name.
I will not open for you.
I will not let you enter past me, says the doorkeeper of this door,
unless you tell my name.
Ox of Geb is your name.
You know us;
pass by us, then.
I will not let you tread on me, says the floor of this Hall of the Two Truths.
And why, then?
I am pure.
Because you do not know the names of your feet with which you would tread on me.
Tell them to me, then.
Image of Min is the name of my right foot;
*Wenpepet* of Hathor is the name of my left foot.
You know us;
enter past us, then.
I will not announce you, says the doorkeeper of this Hall of the Two Truths,
unless you tell my name.
Knower of Hearts, Searcher of Bodies is your name.
To whom, then, shall I announce you? Who is the god who is in his hour?
You shall tell it to the Interpreter of the Two Lands.
Who is he?
The Interpreter of the Two Lands is Thoth.
Come, says Thoth.
Why have you come?
I have come here to be announced.
What is your condition?
I am pure of wrongdoing.
I have kept myself from the strife of those who are in their days.
I am not among them.
To whom, then, shall I announce you? Who is the god who is in his hour?
You shall tell it to the Interpreter of the Two Lands.
Who is he?
The Interpreter of the Two Lands is Thoth.
Come, says Thoth.
Why have you come?
I have come here to be announced.
What is your condition?
I am pure of wrongdoing.
I have kept myself from the strife of those who are in their days.
I am not among them.
To whom, then, shall I announce you?
You shall announce me to the one whose roof is fire, whose walls are living cobras, whose floor is flood-water.
Who is that?
It is Osiris.
Proceed, then;
behold, you are announced.
Your bread is from the Wedjat-eye,
your beer is from the Wedjat-eye,
invocation offerings come forth for you on earth from the Wedjat-eye, so he says, the Osiris [...], justified.
To be done as it happens in this Hall of the Two Truths:
this spell is to be said [by one who is] clean and pure, dressed in clothes, shod in white sandals, painted with black eye-paint, anointed with myrrh,
with cattle, fowl, incense, bread, beer and vegetables offered for him.
And you shall make this image, which is in writing, on a clean floor with ochre, overlaid with [the soil of] a field on which neither pigs nor goats have trodden.
As for one for whom this book is made, he will flourish,
and his children will flourish;
he will not be in want,
for he will be a confidant of the king and his court.
A shens-loaf, a jug, a pezen-loaf and a great portion of meat will be given to him on the altar of the great god.
He will not be turned back at any gate of the West;
he will be ushered in with the kings of Upper and Lower Egypt,
and he will be in the following of Osiris.
Truly correct, a million times.

It was the king's son Hordjedef who found it in a chest of secrets, in the god's own writing, in the temple of Wenut, lady of Wenu, when he was travelling south to make an inspection of the temples in the fields and in the mounds of the gods.
to Osiris in Heni.
The first gateway.
'Upside-down of Face, Many of Forms' is the keeper of the first gateway.
'Eavesdropper' is the name of the one who guards it.
'Wailing of Voice' is the name of the herald in it.
The second gateway.
'Outstretched of Brow' is the name of the keeper of the second gateway.
'Travelling Face' is the name of the one who guards it.
'Blazing One' is the name of the herald in it.
The third gateway.
'Who Eats the Putrefaction of His Hindquarters' is the keeper of the third gateway.
'Watchful of Face' is the name of the one who guards it.
'Curser' is the name of the herald in it.
The fourth gateway.
'Who Repels the Face, Loud of Voice' is the keeper of the fourth gateway.
'Wakeful of Heart' is the name of the one who guards it.
'Great One Who Repels the Aggressor' is the name of the herald in it.
The fifth gateway.
'Who Lives on Worms' is the keeper of the fifth gateway.
'Akhebu' is the name of the one who guards it.
'Hippopotamus Face, Raging of Onslaught' is the name of the herald in it.
The sixth gateway.
'Who Scoops Bread (?), Raging of Voice' is the keeper of the sixth gateway.
'Who Brings the Face' is the name of the one who guards it.
'Keen of Face, He of the Pool' is the name of the herald in it.
The seventh gateway.
'Who Cuts Them Down' is the keeper of the seventh gateway.
'Loud of Voice' is the name of the one who guards it.
'Who Repels the Face of the Destroyers' is the name of the herald in it.

O you gateways, you who attend to the gateways for Osiris, who guard their gateways, who report the affairs of the Two Lands to Osiris every day: the Osiris [...], justified, knows you and knows your names.
The Osiris [...], justified, was born in Rosetau;
'She who kindles flames, who quenches the burning, sharp of flame, swift of hand, who kills without enquiry, past whom none goes for fear of her harm (?)' is your name.
'He Who Protects His Body' is the name of her doorkeeper.
Uncover your faces, take off your headcloths when you meet me, for [I am] the likeness of the great one who is among you.
I have come to make your thin loaves (?).
The bowing centipede (?) shall have no power over me,
the slaughterers shall not come after me,
the adversaries shall not come after me.
I live on the offerings that are among you.
